SecretSpec for Nix

A Nix flake and signed binary cache for SecretSpec, built from upstream stable releases.

Flake source · Build status · Upstream releases

Quick start: accept the flake's cache settings

The flake declares its cache URL and signing key. Accept them for this invocation:

nix run --accept-flake-config github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache -- --help

This authorizes the settings requested by the flake, including trust in this fork's signing key. Without the flag, interactive Nix can prompt for approval. On a multi-user installation, the Nix daemon still enforces its trust policy: an untrusted user may need an administrator to authorize the cache and key using the configuration below. The flag does not bypass daemon restrictions.

To install with the same per-invocation approval:

nix profile add --accept-flake-config github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache

1. Enable the binary cache persistently

Add these settings to your Nix configuration, retaining the default NixOS cache for runtime dependencies:

extra-substituters = https://mausch.github.io/secretspec/cache
extra-trusted-public-keys = mausch-secretspec-1:9RPSefpJCeOFiK0P1g28zfuG1r3p9QgNsIM4G+qU5fI=

For a single-user installation, use ~/.config/nix/nix.conf. For a multi-user installation, have an administrator configure the daemon in /etc/nix/nix.conf and restart it. On NixOS, use:

nix.settings = {
  extra-substituters = [ "https://mausch.github.io/secretspec/cache" ];
  extra-trusted-public-keys = [
    "mausch-secretspec-1:9RPSefpJCeOFiK0P1g28zfuG1r3p9QgNsIM4G+qU5fI="
  ];
};

Apply the NixOS configuration with sudo nixos-rebuild switch. Trusting this key authorizes binaries signed by the maintainer of this fork. A flake cannot silently grant itself that trust.

2. Run or install

With Nix flakes and the nix-command feature enabled:

# Run SecretSpec
nix run github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache -- --help

# Install into your profile
nix profile add github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache

# Open a shell with SecretSpec available
nix develop github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache

The published cache currently targets x86_64-linux. Nix downloads a matching cached build when available; other systems or changed build inputs can require compilation.

Use it from another flake

inputs.secretspec.url = "github:mausch/secretspec/nix-cache";

# Within your outputs, for the desired system:
# secretspec.packages.${system}.default

Keep its pinned Nixpkgs input to match the published derivation. Overriding dependencies can change the store path and cause a cache miss.

Release updates

Every Monday at 06:23 UTC, an automated workflow checks upstream's latest stable release. New releases receive the fork's Nix packaging commits through a rebase. A successful build and test run publishes signed binaries to GitHub Releases and cache metadata to this site. Rebase conflicts or failed builds stop publication and appear in Actions.

For reproducible use, pin a commit or retain your project's flake.lock. Update that pin when you want a newer release.

Cache endpoint: https://mausch.github.io/secretspec/cache
